Editor’s note: This article first appeared on The War Horse , an award-winning nonprofit news organization educating the public on military service. Subscribe to their newsletter . When Hurricane Helene ripped up the East Coast in the fall of 2024, water from the New River flooded towns and destroyed bridges across parts of West Virginia, North Carolina, and Virginia. In Radford, Virginia, floodwaters crested at 31 feet. Just downstream, the river surged into the Radford Army Ammunition Plant, tearing through warehouse doors and washing out more than a dozen storage containers with thousands of gallons of toxic chemicals inside. The Army didn’t warn residents until weeks later about the containers filled with dibutyl phthalate, a key component of rocket propellant that has been linked to cancer and reproductive problems in humans — along with hundreds of gallons of diesel fuel and more than 100,000 pounds of wastewater contaminated with calcium sulfate — that had been washed away in the flood. Officials said later that they assumed the containers would sink to the bottom of the river and floodwaters would dilute any chemical leakage. At least one container, however, washed up on nearby land, where it was partially drained. Two years later, three remain unaccounted for, according to the Virginia Department of Environmental Quality, which found that more than 1,500 gallons had leaked into the environment. Radford Army Ammunition Plant had already been cited earlier in 2024 for discharging excessive levels of pollutants into the New River. It faced a similar penalty in 2023. And in 2022, Virginia environmental regulators listed Radford as the state’s top releaser of toxins. “They’re constantly being cited for putting excessive levels of lead into the water, or other toxic releases into the air, or burning more chemicals than they’re supposed to,” said Alyssa Carpenter, a founder of Citizens for Arsenal Accountability, which advocates for stronger environmental practices at Radford. Radford is also a critical part of the nation’s munitions supply chain: It is the only domestic producer of certain types of propellant used in artillery and rockets. As the Pentagon moves to replenish its depleted munitions stockpile and increase production, it is relying in part on a network of aging Army ammunition plants like Radford, several of which have long histories of violating environmental and safety regulations. A worker inspects rocket tube propellant at Radford Army Ammunition Plant. (Photo by Doris Whipple, courtesy of Radford Army Ammunition Plant) Advocates say the military has too often treated those risks as secondary to production, leaving workers and nearby communities to absorb the consequences. “The track record of the Department of Defense agencies is not good,” said Mathy Stanislaus, who helped oversee toxic cleanup efforts at the Environmental Protection Agency during the Obama administration. “It’s always defense. ‘That’s our mission.’ Everything else is secondary.” Now, advocates worry that pressure to produce more ammunition could intensify the risk to local communities. They argue that the costs of rebuilding America’s arsenal are being borne disproportionately by plant workers and the mostly rural communities surrounding the facilities. “It’s cheap for the military, but it is very expensive for us, for our entire lives,” Carpenter said. “You can’t increase production without increasing the toxic byproducts that come from that production.” An Aging Arsenal As the United States entered World War II, the Army built a network of ammunition plants across the country that became part of Franklin Roosevelt’s “arsenal of democracy.” Many were decommissioned after the war and more closed by the end of the Cold War. Today, much of the defense industrial base is run by private companies, but the Army still manages a network of specialized arsenals, ammunition plants, and maintenance depots, many of which help manufacture, test, and repair missiles, heavy ordnance, and their components, handling work that ranges from creating raw explosive chemicals and rocket propellant to loading warheads and artillery shells. The United States military is running low on several critical munitions. A report from the Center for Strategic and International Studies published this summer estimated that U.S. inventory of Patriot interceptor missiles had fallen from more than 2,300 at the start of the Iran War to around 800 by the end of July. Stocks of THAAD interceptors, which shoot down incoming ballistic missiles, had likewise fallen by nearly half, from roughly 450 before the war. Stocks of THAAD interceptors have reportedly declined by nearly half since the start of the Iran War. (Missile Defense Agency) The strain predates the Iran War, however. U.S. inventories of precision-guided weapons and heavy conventional ordnance stockpiles had already been under pressure from decades of post-Cold War factory consolidation and shipments to allies overseas. Before Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine, the United States produced about 14,000 155 mm artillery shells a month. At times, Ukrainian soldiers were burning through that many rounds in just a few days. And historically, munitions production has often lost out to other priorities in Pentagon budget fights. “When you’re putting together a budget, you can’t just ask for everything,” said Carlton Haelig, who works on defense strategy at the Center for a New American Security. “When there need to be cuts to pay for an extra squadron [of fighter jets] purchased, another set of transport aircraft, surface ships, whatever, the place that is often considered for making those cuts is in the munitions portfolio.” In recent years, however, concern about a potential confrontation with China has pushed the Pentagon to expand munitions production. Last year, the Defense Department established a new council tasked with dramatically increasing production of 14 weapons systems, and it has poured billions of dollars toward accelerating production of 155 mm artillery shells. Environmental advocates worry that pushing more production through aging Army facilities could worsen existing problems with pollution, worker safety, and transparency. “Measured by the number of sites where hazardous substances have been released into the environment, the military is far and away the largest polluter in the United States,” said Lenny Siegel, an expert on military contamination who leads the Center for Public Environmental Oversight. “I see the simple issue of math. If you’re releasing X into the environment now, you’re going to release 10X when you multiply your production by 10.” Justine Barati, a spokesperson for the Army Sustainment Command, which oversees these facilities, disagreed. “The U.S. Army does not, and will never, compromise the safety of our workforce or our surrounding communities to meet production quotas. Protecting our people and the environment is foundational to national security,” she said. “We cannot sustain warfighter readiness without safe, resilient, and compliant installations.” Barati pointed to a sweeping $18 billion modernization effort across these facilities, saying the Army’s “highest priority” in the modernization is to improve environmental compliance and workplace safety. But that project is not scheduled to be completed until 2038, and the Army is already accelerating production at some facilities. “At the same time, the Ukraine war started to get hot and heavy, and we were given the edict that’s like, ‘hurry up and go fast’,” Maj. Gen. John Reim, head of the joint armaments and ammunitions program executive office, told Breaking Defense last year. Marines load an M777 towed 155 mm howitzer into the cargo hold of a plane to send in support of Ukraine’s efforts against the Russian invasion. (Cpl. Austin Fraley/U.S. Marine Corps) EPA records show that all the Army ammunition plants and arsenals involved in producing, testing, or storing weapon components have been cited or flagged for noncompliance by the EPA or state regulators in the past five years. Four of them have been flagged for “significant noncompliance” by the EPA, designating them severe or chronic violators of environmental law. Many of them have also violated state environmental regulations. EPA records show Scranton Army Ammunition Plant in Pennsylvania, for instance, which helps forge steel 155 mm shell bodies, was flagged for violating the Clean Water Act and Clean Air Act multiple times during 2024 and 2025. At the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in 2023, regulators found workers improperly detonated explosives in a detonation chamber, among other issues. At Holston Army Ammunition Plant in Kingsport, Tennessee, BAE Systems, which operates the plant, was fined this October by the Tennessee Department of Environment and Conservation’s air pollution control division for improper record-keeping and reporting of data. Federal and state regulators can inspect and penalize these facilities, but the fines are often small compared with the sheer size and resources of the Defense Department. After EPA inspectors found alleged violations at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant, in 2024, the EPA fined the Army and plant operator American Ordnance just under $40,000 — compare that with a $53 million Army contract American Ordnance was awarded this year for its work at the plant. “The biggest problem is that the Department of Defense is effectively self-regulating,” Stanislaus, the former EPA official, said. “When the rubber hits the road, EPA and state agencies simply do not have the authority to mandate certain activities, everything from preventing harm to doing the cleanup.” A Whistleblower’s Safety Concerns The fire that erupted on a July night in Crane, Indiana, burned for 15 hours. Workers at Crane Army Ammunition Activity, which disposes of old munitions, had been storing mortar rounds outdoors in wooden crates beneath a tarp in the baking sun. Temperatures had climbed into the high 90s for several days. The rounds contained red phosphorus, which can generate heat and flammable gases as it degrades. On the evening of July 6, 2022, nearly 115,000 pounds of red phosphorus ignited, sending flames and smoke billowing into the sky. A fire resulting from improperly stored mortar rounds erupted at Naval Weapons Station Crane in 2022. (Photo courtesy of Rick Ward) What happened before and after illustrates how difficult it can be to hold these facilities accountable. Three years earlier, Rick Ward, the newly hired safety chief at Crane Army Ammunition Activity, which is housed at Naval Weapons Station Crane, had concerns with safety at the facility. A safety program for controlling hazardous substances was not fully implemented. Hazardous processes weren’t properly classified. Slings used to move heavy explosives didn’t have current certifications. Ward pointed to an earlier explosion at Crane, in 2013, that sent five people to the hospital. An OSHA inspection afterward identified three dozen safety violations, and an Army “lessons learned” report cited a lack of clear safety procedures. Ward worried that the safety culture at Crane hadn’t changed. He began bringing concerns up with his supervisors, according to documents he shared with The War Horse. “Can you imagine taking over as a safety director and knowing that you’ve been handed 36 OSHA violations that never got corrected?” he said. The year before Ward arrived, EPA had also cited Naval Weapons Station Crane — the base where Crane Army Ammunition Activity is housed — for improperly storing hazardous waste. But Ward felt his concerns were not being taken seriously. So in 2020, he filed an anonymous complaint with OSHA. Rick Ward, the former civilian safety chief at Crane Army Ammunition Activity, was fired after he brought up safety concerns. (Photo courtesy of Rick Ward) Because of COVID-related restrictions, OSHA asked the Army to investigate the allegations itself. Ironically, Crane leaders assigned Ward to conduct the investigation. About an hour after Ward submitted his report, he said, he was put on administrative leave. He was fired several months later, according to a statement from his lawyers. Ward has struggled to find work ever since. Crane barred him from the installation, and the Air Force, where he serves as a reserve officer, revoked his security clearance. “It’s really hard to get a job when you’ve been on the front page of every newspaper in Indiana,” he said. Barati, the Army Sustainment Command spokesperson, disputed Ward’s account. “The Army did not retaliate against Mr. Rick Ward in any form or manner. The Army takes workplace safety very seriously and welcomes safety concern feedback from all our employees,” she said. Many of Ward’s concerns were later substantiated. A whistleblower investigation partially or fully upheld five of his eight allegations. Among them: Crane did not maintain an accurate list of locations where hazardous work occurred and lacked a complete safety plan for controlling and handling hazardous substances. EPA inspections in 2023 and 2024 found additional problems at Naval Weapons Station Crane. Inspectors reported materials were still stored in ways that could create fire risks, hazardous materials lacked proper labeling, open containers held corrosive waste, and hazardous waste was kept onsite for more than three times the legal time limit. “If you mislabel a particular compound, and you put it into a vessel that cannot handle the corrosiveness of that, then it leaks through that vessel and contaminates the ground,” Stanislaus said. “Terrible things can happen.” Last fall, EPA notified Naval Weapons Station Crane that it planned to assess nearly $250,000 in penalties for the violations. That is a significant EPA penalty. But for Crane, it’s barely a line item in the budget. Toxins in the Air Not long after Alyssa Carpenter graduated from Virginia Tech in 2017, just a few miles from the Radford Army Ammunition Plant, she had to have her thyroid removed. She was 26, otherwise healthy, and had no family history of thyroid cancer. Doctors told her the gland was covered in suspicious nodules. Carpenter cannot say for sure what caused her condition. But as a student at Virginia Tech, she had advocated for better environmental controls at the plant, and she worries the chemicals the plant releases into the environment may have played a role in her illness. Alyssa Carpenter worries her thyroid condition is linked to toxic chemicals from Radford Army Ammunition Plant. (Photo courtesy of Alyssa Carpenter) For decades, Radford and other military facilities have disposed of old munitions and production waste by burning or detonating them in the open, releasing toxic gases, particulate matter, and volatile organic compounds into the air. The United States generally banned open burning and open detonation of hazardous waste in 1980 but created an exception for explosive waste that could not safely be treated another way. That exception has allowed the practice to continue at military and civilian munition facilities. In 2025, 45 years after the ban, 64 public and private facilities across the United States were still allowed to burn or detonate hazardous waste. Residents around Radford have long raised concerns about thyroid disease in the area, though a 2022 review of cancer-registry data by VPM News , a local NPR station, found mixed evidence of unusually high rates. What is clear is that the plant regularly releases hazardous pollutants into the air. According to EPA data, in 2024, Radford released into the air — along with other chemicals — 19,000 pounds of ammonia, which reacts with the atmosphere to create a fine particulate matter known to cause respiratory distress, and more than 900 pounds of lead compounds or lead, a neurotoxin with no known safe level of human exposure. EPA requires facilities to report lead emissions if they exceed just 100 pounds a year. Barati, the Army Sustainment Command spokesperson, said that Radford had reduced the amount of waste treated by open burning by more than 50% since 2017. She also pointed to a new energetic waste incinerator under construction at the facility that will ultimately replace the need for open burning. The incinerator, originally scheduled to be completed in 2025 , will not be operational until 2027, Barati said. Open burns are subject to environmental limits, and facilities are supposed to account for wind patterns and other factors to make burns safer. But those safeguards can be difficult to enforce. At Crane, for instance, EPA inspectors cited the facility in 2023 for conducting burns when its own records showed weather conditions outside permitted limits. (Crane officials told the EPA weather was recorded at a different time of day and that the weather was in parameters when it conducted the burns). Technology has changed since the U.S. allowed an exception for the open burning or detonation of military munitions in 1980. Many other countries, including Germany and Canada, have banned open burning and open detonation of hazardous waste, and military munitions are disposed of in contained burn chambers or closed incinerators. In 2024, the EPA proposed new rules that would further restrict the practice and push facilities toward safer alternative technologies. But the rulemaking has stalled. An EPA spokesperson told The War Horse that the agency plans to finalize the regulations by the end of this year. A bulldozer shovels refuse in an open air burn pit in Balad, Iraq in 2004. The military moved away from open burning at overseas bases after troops began developing rare cancers and lung conditions. (U.S. Army) The military has moved away from open-air waste burning in recent years at overseas bases. For decades, troops stationed in Iraq, Afghanistan, and other countries burned everything from medical waste and plastics to old explosives in open burn pits. Military officials defended the pits as a practical necessity in remote war zones. Like the residents of some communities near ammunition plants in the U.S., service members at bases with burn pits breathed in toxic air containing particulate matter that irritated their throats and lungs, and heavy metals that accumulated in their tissues. When they came home from deployment, they began developing rare cancers and other diseases. But as veterans reported respiratory illnesses, cancers, and other health problems after breathing in the smoke, public pressure grew. The military eventually curtailed the use of burn pits overseas, and Congress passed the PACT Act in 2022 , expanding VA benefits for millions of veterans exposed to the toxic substances during military service — but there are no such benefits for civilians exposed to domestic burn pits. For Carpenter, that history shows the military can change when the risks become impossible to ignore. “If it’s toxic for service members, then it’s going to be toxic for community members as well,” she said. This article from   The War Horse   was edited by Paul Szoldra, fact-checked by Jess Rohan, and copy-edited by Mitchell Hansen-Dewar.

民進黨新北市長參選人蘇巧慧競選總部發言人劉芳宇（圖）5日針對媒體公布最新民調指蘇巧慧支持度領先對手李四川一事表示，證明蘇巧慧始終堅持正面陽光的選戰方向，得到多數新北市民的認同。（蘇巧慧競總提供）中央社記者王鴻國傳真 115年11月5日
（中央社記者王鴻國、黃旭昇新北5日電）根據媒體公佈民調，蘇巧慧支持度領先李四川近15個百分點。蘇巧慧表示，感謝越來越多民眾支持；李四川競辦表示，內部民調數據，李四川仍維持穩定領先。
民進黨新北市長參選人蘇巧慧競選總部發言人劉芳宇今天針對鏡新聞公布最新民調指出，蘇巧慧支持度47.7%，領先李四川32.8%達14.9個百分點。證明蘇巧慧始終堅持正面陽光的選戰方向，得到多數新北市民的認同。
蘇巧慧接受媒體聯訪時表示，真的很感謝，從民調的數字來看「顯示有越來越多的人站在我們這邊、支持我們」，也期待蘇巧慧及新北隊，可以為新北市帶來新氣象、新時代。
她表示，會用誠懇的態度，以陽光、正面、講願景的態度，繼續完成最後一哩路。剩下 20 多天，一起努力，迎接新北市的新時代，蘇巧慧就會是新時代最適合的新北市市長。
國民黨新北市長參選人李四川競選辦公室表示，對於鏡新聞今天公布新北市長選舉民調，根據內部民調數據，李四川仍維持穩定領先，雖今天公布的民調樣本，與新北過往真實選舉結構呈現極大落差，但團隊對於選情仍會持續審慎面對。
李四川競辦表示，蘇巧慧陣營看到民調領先即發布新聞稿攻擊李四川，暴露蘇巧慧傲慢的真實面貌，雖然蘇巧慧陣營持續以龐大網軍側翼資源進行選舉攻擊，放任網路出征霸凌的文化，甚至以人身攻擊、言詞羞辱李四川。
李四川競辦表示，李四川不會改變正面、正當的選舉方式，會持續深入29區基層，以拿得出的政績、做得到的政見，持續爭取不分顏色市民朋友的支持。呼籲大家用選票支持老實做人、踏實做事的李四川，這一票不只是給認真做事的人肯定，更是要一同拒絕抹黑攻擊、網路霸凌的負面選舉文化。
鏡新聞今天公布新北市長民調，由鏡新聞委託大地民意研究公司進行，調查時間為11月1日至2日，訪問對象為戶籍設於新北市且年滿20歲以上的民眾，採用市話訪問，依新北市各行政區人口比例抽出電話號碼，共完成有效樣本1087份，在95%信心水準下，抽樣誤差為正負2.97個百分點。（編輯：林恕暉）1151105

content:
独家：众议院中国委员会推动空军智库削减 - Breaking Defense
2025 年 4 月 21 日，在马里兰州安德鲁斯联合基地举行的“了解中国航空航天”活动中，中国航天研究院的扑克牌放在桌子上。（美国空军照片/高级飞行员 Gianluca Ciccopiedi）
华盛顿——众议院中国问题特别委员会的议员们正在敦促空军就其以北京为中心的智囊团计划缩减规模的问题寻求答案，并警告说，该组织产出的任何减少都可能影响美国的国家安全。
根据《Breaking Defense》独家看到的信函副本，中国航天研究院（CASI）的使命“资源不足”，“可能会损害军事领导人和文职决策者理解”北京航空航天战略和军事实力的能力。
这封信是写给空军部长特洛伊·梅克（Troy Meink）的，由共和党主席约翰·穆勒纳尔（John Moolenaar）和民主党资深议员罗·卡纳（Ro Khanna）签署，信中要求在 11 月 20 日之前进行简报，以提供有关 CASI“资源和人事决策”的信息。
众议院议员在信中表示，由于中国不断发展的航空航天能力和“在印太地区的侵略活动”，CASI 技能的“任何潜在损失”都“尤其令人担忧”。立法者赞扬 CASI 的工作，表示该研究所“内部专业知识”的替代方案可能需要空军和其他政府实体“花费大量资源从外部供应商购买合同专业知识”。
鉴于中国人民解放军的空中和太空力量迅速发展，立法者表示，相关分析的减少“尤其令人担忧”，并且可能会影响美国的威慑力，因为人们对潜在的台湾之战的担忧日益加剧。
信中说：“随着解放军继续扩大其航空航天能力，我们对了解这些进步的需求将继续增长。”一名空军发言人告诉《Breaking Defense》，空军“将直接向委员会做出回应”。
这封信是在 9 月份透露空军计划裁减 CASI 的 10 名文职人员之后发出的。尽管空军坚持其主要的以中国为中心的智库将保持开放并由军事人员运作，但其主任布伦丹·马尔瓦尼在接受《Breaking Defense》采访时强调，取消文职人员将在功能上关闭该研究所。
赞助帖子、网络和数字战争
当任务硬件无法发展时，边缘计算就会失败
回报是更快的技术插入，避免供应商锁定，以及更多的自主、传感器、武器和任务增长空间。
CASI 由马尔瓦尼大约十年前创立，利用从普通话翻译过来的开源信息，定期发布有关北京空军和太空部队的研究报告。该研究所的出版物和培训课程被视为对更广泛的军事政策界进行有关中国空天力量教育的宝贵资源，这促使专家们谴责了CASI预期的裁员计划。
马尔瓦尼此前曾对《突破防御》表示，如果没有民间专家，“我们所做的研究或翻译的想法是不可信的”。
马尔瓦尼解释说，该智囊团的文职职位正在转变为无资金资助状态，这意味着工作人员将继续工作，直到他们调到财政部其他地方的不同职位。

EXCLUSIVE: House China committee pushes Air Force on think tank cuts - Breaking Defense
China Aerospace Studies Institute playing cards rest on a table during the Understanding China’s Aerospace event at Joint Base Andrews, Md., April 21, 2025. (U.S. Air Force photo/Senior Airman Gianluca Ciccopiedi)
WASHINGTON — Lawmakers on the House Select Committee on China are pushing the Air Force for answers about a planned downsizing of its Beijing-focused think tank, warning that any reduction in the group’s output could impact America’s national security.
“Under-resourcing” the mission of the China Aerospace Studies Institute (CASI) “could risk undermining the ability of military leaders and civilian policymakers to understand” Beijing’s aerospace strategy and military prowess, according to a copy of the letter viewed exclusively by Breaking Defense.
Addressed to Air Force Secretary Troy Meink and signed by Republican Chairman John Moolenaar and Democratic Ranking Member Ro Khanna, the letter requests a briefing by Nov. 20 to provide information on “resourcing and personnel decisions” for CASI.
In their letter, House lawmakers say that “[a]ny potential loss” of CASI’s skills “is particularly worrisome” due to China’s burgeoning aerospace capabilities and “aggressive activities in the Indo-Pacific region.” Praising CASI’s work, the lawmakers say that alternatives to the institute’s “in-house expertise” would likely require the Air Force and other government entities “to expend considerable resources to purchase contracted expertise from external vendors.”
Given the rapidly advancing air and space power of the Chinese People’s Liberation Army (PLA), the lawmakers say that diminishing relevant analysis is “particularly concerning” and could impact American deterrence, as fears mount over a potential battle for Taiwan.
“As the PLA continues to expand its aerospace capabilities, our need to understand these advancements will continue to grow,” the letter says. An Air Force spokesperson told Breaking Defense that the service “will respond directly to the committee.”
The letter comes after it was revealed in September that the Air Force planned to axe CASI’s 10-member civilian workforce. While the Air Force maintained its premier China-focused think tank would remain open and operate with military personnel, its director, Brendan Mulvaney, stressed in an interview with Breaking Defense that the elimination of its civilian staff would functionally shutter the institute.

The payoff is quicker tech insertion, avoiding vendor lock, and more room for autonomy, sensors, weapons, and mission growth.
Founded by Mulvaney roughly a decade ago, CASI regularly publishes research on Beijing’s air and space forces, drawing on open-source information translated from Mandarin. The institute’s publications and training courses are seen as valuable resources for educating the broader military policy community on Chinese air and space power, prompting experts to denounce CASI’s expected downsizing.
“The idea that you could do research or the translations that we’re doing is not credible” without civilian experts, Mulvaney previously told Breaking Defense.
Mulvaney explained that the think tank’s civilian posts are being converted to an unfunded status, meaning that staffers will continue to work until they are moved to a different role elsewhere in the Department of the Air Force — and once they leave, their positions cannot be backfilled. CASI’s current commitments stretch until around March and will largely function as usual until then, but after that the institute’s fate becomes more unclear, according to Mulvaney.
News of the CASI cuts raised questions about similar efforts run by the Army, Navy and Marine Corps, though spokespeople for each service previously told Breaking Defense that there are no planned changes for their respective Beijing-focused programs.

content:
谷歌前首席执行官埃里克·施密特创立的智囊团的一份新报告量化了美国国防工业基地在关键稀土矿物方面依赖中国的严峻现实。它还详细说明了如果这种微妙的供应关系破裂，哪些武器系统可能面临最大的影响。这份白皮书专门从特别竞争研究项目中获得，利用供应链科技公司 Exiger 的人工智能情报来评估有多少由国家物品识别号 (NIIN) 识别的独特组件含有关键矿物质，例如锑、镓、锗和钨。美国的武器库依赖于稀土的稳定供应，尤其是最先进的武器。美国空军 摄影：Tech Sgt.托马斯·巴利科技。中士。 Thomas Barley 通过对近 900 万个零件和 3,000 个美国军用武器系统的评估，该公司在 1,400 个武器系统中发现了 28,000 多个独特组件仅含有这四种稀土。由于近期的危机，这些部分的隔离尤其重要：中国出口管制的暂停将于 11 月到期。根据白皮书，武器部署计划以及战备和保障活动很有可能受到干扰。然而，Exiger 首席战略和全球事务官基特·康克林 (Kit Conklin) 表示，危机已经到来。
在接受 TWZ 采访时，他指出日本正面临着生产停顿的前景，因为今年早些时候中国切断了一些稀土供应超过 80%。康克林表示：“毫无疑问，目前对于许多试图获得中国批准的许可证但没有获得许可证的公司来说，这是一场危机。” “因此，当前的生产存在真正的风险，当我考虑我们的生产和规模扩张时，无论是无人机工业基地还是试图将我们的拦截器产能扩大到每年 1,000、2,000、3,000 个拦截器，我的意思是，这些都是我们面临的真正的瓶颈，正在影响我们现在向作战人员提供这些拦截器的能力。”数据显示，供应链和制造中断风险最大的武器系统之一是至关重要的弗吉尼亚级潜艇，它需要 300 多个含有四种元素的关键 NIIN，其中包括 190 个需要锗的部件。弗吉尼亚号（SSN 774）是弗吉尼亚级的领舰，是美国海军快速攻击潜艇部队的骨干力量。美国海军照片由通用动力电船公司拍摄 美国海军锗是锌矿石的副产品，用于光学、夜视系统、EO/IR 设备等。一月份，五角大楼宣布投资 1800 万美元建设位于圣路易斯的美国唯一的锗生产设施。
犹他州乔治市将在未具体说明的期限内将炼油能力扩大“七倍”，达到每年 20 吨以上。中国控制着全球约 68% 的精炼锗。它对用于半导体和太阳能电池，尤其是先进雷达的镓的控制力要大得多，控制着高达 99% 的产量。每艘弗吉尼亚级潜艇都需要 50 个含有镓的独特部件。中国控制着大约一半的锑产量，用于硬化弹药以及制造光学和电子产品；高达80%的钨供应量，用于制造工具、弹头和耐热部件。虽然它

【原文 English Original】
A new report from the think tank founded by former Google CEO Eric Schmidt quantifies the grim realities of the U.S. defense industrial base’s dependence on China for critical rare earth minerals. It also details which weapons systems might face the most impact if that delicate supply relationship breaks down. The white paper, exclusively obtained from the Special Competitive Studies Project, uses AI intelligence from the supply chain tech firm Exiger to assess how many unique components, identified by National Item Identification Number, or NIIN, contain critical minerals, such as antimony, gallium, germanium and tungsten. America’s arsenal depends on a steady flow of rare earths, and especially its most advanced weapons. U.S. Air Force photo by Tech Sgt. Thomas Barley Tech. Sgt. Thomas Barley From an assessment of almost nine million parts and 3,000 U.S. military weapon systems, the company identified more than 28,000 unique components  across 1,400 weapons systems containing just these four rare earths. The isolation of these parts is relevant in particular because of a near-term crisis: the expiration of a suspension on Chinese export controls set to take effect in November. Disruption to weapons fielding plans, as well as operational readiness and sustainment activities, according to the white paper, is very much a possibility. Yet according to Kit Conklin, chief strategy and global affairs officer at Exiger, the crisis is already here.  In an interview with TWZ , he pointed to Japan, which is facing the prospect of a manufacturing halt after China choked off supply of some rare earths to the tune of more than 80% earlier this year. “There’s no question that right now it’s a crisis for a lot of companies that are trying to get licenses approved by China and just not getting the licenses,” Conklin said. “So there’s real risk to current production, and when I think about us and scaling, whether it’s the drone industrial base or trying to scale our interceptor capacity to 1,000, 2,000, 3,000 interceptors a year, I mean, these are real choke points that we have that are impacting our ability to deliver these to the warfighter right now.” Among the weapons systems most at risk for supply chain and manufacturing disruption, according to the data, is the vital Virginia -class submarine, which requires more than 300 critical NIINs containing the four elements, including 190 parts requiring germanium. USS Virginia (SSN 774), the leader of the Virginia class that serves as the backbone of the U.S. Navy’s fast attack submarine force. U.S. Navy photo by General Dynamics Electric Boat U.S. Navy Germanium, used in optics, night vision systems, EO/IR equipment and more, is a byproduct of zinc ore . In January, the Pentagon announced an $18 million investment in the country’s only germanium production facility in St. George, Utah to expand refining capacity “sevenfold” to more than 20 metric tons annually by an unspecified deadline. China controls some 68% of the world’s refined germanium. It has a far greater chokehold on gallium, used in semiconductors and solar cells, and especially advanced radars, controlling up to 99% of production . Each Virginia -class sub requires 50 unique parts containing gallium. China controls about half the production of antimony, used to harden ammunition and to manufacture optics and electronics; and up to 80% of the supply of tungsten, used in manufacturing tools, warheads and heat-resistant components. While it doesn’t break down components by weight, the report notes that the rare earth requirements for the Virginia -class sub are also considerable by mass: each sub required 9,200 pounds of the elements, while an F-35 Joint Strike Fighter jet requires 900 pounds. Special Competitive Studies Project The Virginia -class submarine is America’s only in-production fast-attack nuclear-powered sub that has been in service since 2004. Twenty three of these critical vessels are in service today , or roughly half of the total planned program, with the remaining boats yet to be built. It’s notable in the context of the paper because it has multiple points of exposure to supply chain disruption. Another of these exposure points: its 1,700 mission or safety-critical parts requiring casting, forging or extrusion. As the report lays out, supply chain bottlenecks around limited metal casting, forging and extruding capacity are delaying production timelines and putting manufacturing at risk. China, again, produces about half of the world’s casting output and “is often the sole option for large castings,” the paper found. The analysis shows that more than half, or nearly 8,000, unique supply items containing steel castings have delivery lead times of more than 36 weeks. More than 9,400 items containing extruded aluminum, about 47% of these parts, have lead times that long. A large metal casting for a port crane. Voestalpine Foundry Group “ Virginia -class submarines, already threatened by U.S. reliance on China for critical minerals, are reportedly also three years behind schedule, potentially due in part to the lack of domestic large-scale casting capacity,” the report finds. An analysis of Navy construction timelines published earlier this year does indeed find that 10 of the 12 Virginia subs now under construction face delays of 36-44 months. Alarmingly, a recent war game simulation found that the U.S. could not replace ships, planes and missiles lost to combat specifically due to casting and forging shortfalls, the report notes. That’s despite a $2 billion Pentagon initiative launched in 2024 aimed at revitalizing this industry. Beyond submarines, the report shows that aircraft, including some of the nation’s workhorse fighter jets, face outsized production and sustainment risk due to rare-earth elements and casting/forging dependencies. The B-2 Spirit bomber – the nation’s only nuclear-armed stealth bomber until fielding begins on the B-21 Raider sometime next year – requires 782 parts containing the four rare-earth elements isolated in the report. Special Competitive Studies Project The F/A-18 Hornet family of fighters flown by the Navy and Marine Corps, including the Navy’s Growler electronic warfare variant, tops the list for dependency on steel castings, with 3,800 individual parts requiring the process. Following is the KC-135 Stratotanker, with 2,570 parts. All 10 of the systems requiring the most metal castings for production are aircraft, the analysis shows. The legacy Hornet and the KC-135 have been out of production for decades, while the Navy’s Super Hornet will see its production line go cold in 2027. Any ongoing demand for castings for these systems would thus be in spares and repair parts. Special Competitive Studies Project Military aircraft also represent the highest-need category among weapons systems requiring cadmium plating, a process used to make aerospace components corrosion-resistant.  The domestic supplier base has shrunk due to EPA safety limitations established in 2008. All of the top 10 weapons systems requiring the most cadmium-plated parts are aircraft, with the KC-135 topping the list with 2,780 unique components. The C-130 Hercules transport, B-52 Stratofortress bomber and Galaxy C-5 transport all have more than 2,000 parts. Special Competitive Studies Project The B-52, which is undergoing a service life extension to take it into the 2050s – past its century mark – may run into modernization delays not only over cadmium-plated and steel-casted components, but also due to overly rigid military specifications, which increase lead time and delays. The white paper cites the bomber’s rib airfoil and fuel vent valve components, which both have lead times of more than 400 days due in part to production being burdened with dozens of mil-spec compliance requirements, which the authors say have not kept pace with today’s commercial practices. “The requirement for a part to meet so many mil-specs, if not reasonably necessary, may limit the number of possible suppliers of that part, potentially increasing its lead time and bottlenecking production,” they write. “For the B-52, this could inhibit current modernization efforts intended to keep the airplane operational through the 2050s.” A B-52H Stratofortress undergoing programmed depot maintenance is towed into a hangar at Tinker Air Force Base, Oklahoma, July 28, 2025. U.S. Air Force photo by Paul Shirk Paul Shirk A final risk the paper addresses is workforce shortages and dangers from limited suppliers creating single points of failure. Across defense, the number of small suppliers has decreased by 43% in the last decade, it notes. It cites, as a case study, the February 2025 fire that forced the closure of SPS Technologies in Jenkintown, Penn. – a fastener maker that produced components for more than 1,000 weapons systems and was deemed critical for 90, including the Nimitz -class carrier, the F/A-18 fighter and the M1 Abrams tank. For systems including the Tomahawk Land Attack Missile and the MH-60 Black Hawk helicopter, the facility was a single-source supplier. With operations offline until at least 2028, the supply chain has been “actively disrupted” due to the outage of just one facility, according to the paper. “This case underscores the risk of single sourcing in the defense industrial base and the need to qualify alternate sources to avoid such significant chokepoints,” the authors write. The paper hails work that has already begun to invest in domestic critical minerals production and shore up the defense industrial base. But it does hint that these efforts may be too late to avoid a crash if China shuts off or severely reduces exports. The paper notes that, on average, it takes the U.S. 29 years to open a new mine. The U.S. has one established domestic mine: The Mountain Pass Rare Earth Mine and Processing Facility, just outside of Las Vegas. Initially established in 1952 and reopened in 2018 after a long hiatus, it now produces more than 50,000 tons of rare earth oxides annually . Last year, for the first time in seven decades, a new domestic rare-earth mine opened in Wyoming , stating plans to start producing ores extracted from coal, including gallium and germanium, by 2029 . Production is projected to total 456 tons of rare earths per year. The project had been in development for more than a decade before opening.  The Mountain Pass Rare Earth Mine and Processing Facility. MP Materials Conklin said a July executive order aimed at developing domestic production of rare earths while collecting data on what elements systems required created opportunities for smart policy creation – perhaps in the next National Defense Authorization Act – around holistically attacking the problem.  “I would love for us to figure out a way to get out of thinking about these supply chain risks system by system. We tend to have disparate requirements to look at the nuclear triad or subs or interceptors,” he said. “I think with the executive order that came out earlier this year, there’s a real opportunity for Congress to legislate on some of these issues beyond just figuring out what the risk [is] for antimony in the sub industrial base, and thinking about it a little bit more holistically.” One potential solution he proposed: an agency within the executive branch (led, perhaps, by a critical minerals czar) who can coordinate production needs and resourcing and develop the most efficient pathways to secure needed materials. There are few weapons that are not impacted by the scarcity of robust sources for rare earths. RTX While no U.S. defense manufacturer has yet publicly cited manufacturing disruptions due to rare earth availability, signs are increasing that the federal government is taking supply concerns seriously. In addition to Project Vault , a $12 billion White House initiative announced in February that would create a strategic stockpile of rare earths akin to existing stockpiles of critical medical supplies and petroleum, the U.S. Army has begun extending long-term leases on military land to companies seeking to build critical mineral processing facilities. Conklin said he doesn’t anticipate major changes in rare earth exports between now and the end of the year, describing the U.S.-China supply relationship as “in a bit of a détente.” That said, with new policies pending, we could be only days away from new revelations about the extent of the impact of these materials on the defense manufacturing enterprise. Contact the editor: Tyler@twz.com The post These Are The U.S. Weapons Most At Risk In The Looming Rare Earths Supply Crisis appeared first on TWZ .

Nurnisa Kurban for Uyghur Academic Foundation
Nurnisa Kurban is organizing this fundraiser to benefit Uyghur Academic Foundation.
Nurnisa Kurban for Uyghur Academic Foundation
Uyghur Cultural Preservation and Survival Through Education
The Uyghur people have been persecuted and subjected to repressive Chinese government policies in their Indigenous homeland of East Turkestan for many years. It is estimated that up to three million Uyghurs have been interned, imprisoned, and enslaved in detention centers, prisons, and forced labor facilities throughout China since 2017.
In 2021, the Uyghur Tribunal found that China was committing genocide and other crimes against humanity against Uyghurs. In 2022, the United Nations also concluded that China was committing human rights violations against Uyghurs amounting to crimes against humanity. Countries including the United States, Canada, the Netherlands, Czech Republic, United Kingdom, Lithuania, Belgium, and France have all declared a genocide in East Turkestan. Despite these declarations of genocide and related reports by various human rights organizations, atrocities against Uyghurs continue today with very limited international recognition and accountability.
During this time of ongoing genocide and cultural erasure in their Indigenous homeland, Uyghurs of the diaspora are working to preserve their culture and identity as a matter of survival. Uyghur education has been eradicated by the Chinese State, Uyghur texts are forbidden and in danger of being eliminated, and the Uyghur language itself is prohibited.
Uyghur scholars, linguists, and other specialists in the diaspora worldwide serve on the Uyghur Language and Education Committee of the Uyghur Academy to preserve the work of Uyghur intellectuals who have been persecuted and forcibly disappeared. This work has been ongoing since 2009 and is continuing to expand.
The Committee has created standards-aligned K-5 textbooks, which include classic and contemperory Uyghur literature, poetry, historical texts, and biographies for Uyghur children to learn about their own culture and identity in their native language. The Committee is seeking funding to expand and revise the existing K-5 textbooks, create teacher’s edition textbooks for educators, and design supplemental resources. They also hope to develop Middle and High School textbooks and related supplemental resources. To effectively implement these educational materials, they would also like to provide training for teachers.
Please consider supporting this urgent work of the Uyghur Academic Foundation as a matter of cultural survival for future generations of the Uyghur people.

万斯此前一直对用战争手段解决伊朗问题持保留态度图像来源: Tom Brenner/REUTERS
（德国之声中文网）在共和党输掉中期选举之后，副总统万斯表示：“如果你想争辩说这一切是值得的——即为了这场战争而失去参议院六年的控制权是值得的——那你就尽管去做……”
“但人人都知道我们为什么输了。任何关于我们未来走向的坦诚讨论，都必须从这一点出发，”这位美国副总统周三在社交媒体平台X上写道。“我们失败的原因就是这场（伊朗）战争。总统本人昨晚也这么说了。”
共和党在11月3日的中期选举惨败，将众议院和参议院的控制权拱手让给民主党；此次选举也被视为对特朗普各项政策的一次“全民公投”。
特朗普与以色列在2月份共同发动的对伊战争在美国民众中极不受欢迎，因为战争推高了燃油价格，而且这场冲突目前看来还远未结束。
当被问及万斯的分析时，特朗普表示：“我认为这在很大程度上是对的，因为它在短期内确实推高了汽油价格。”但这位美国总统也坚称对伊开战的决定是正确的。特朗普表示，如果再次面临同样的选择，他仍会做出同样的决定，并继续称这场战争是“值得的”。
万斯和美国国务卿卢比奥都被视为2028年共和党总统候选人提名的有力竞争者。
根据美国法律，美国总统无法竞选第三个任期，因此特朗普无法再次参加竞选。此前对于谁可能成为共和党领袖的继任者，特朗普一直未予明确表态。
周三在白宫宴会厅施工现场面对摄像机时谈及此事时，特朗普说，“也许他（万斯）不会参选。我不知道谁会参选”。

北京香山论坛多国代表对军用人工智能的潜在风险深表担忧。在美中两国准备举行高层会晤之际，武器自主化正急剧压缩决策时间，大国在此类技术管控上的分歧再度引发广泛讨论。
在欧盟释放信号，表示愿意让加拿大以“准成员”身份成为其特殊伙伴后，美国总统特朗普对此发出嘲讽，并表示，这一设想属于“敌对行为”。
周一，中共为前总书记江泽民举行百岁冥诞纪念大会。周二，前总理朱镕基的遗体在八宝山公墓火化，天安门等地降半旗致哀。江泽民与朱镕基留给习近平怎样的遗产？习近平能否借助已经逝去的时代安抚当下的民心，进一步巩固自己的权力？
911恐袭事件迎来25周年纪念。纽约世贸中心大厦轰然倒塌的影像，是历史的见证，记录了当时惊心动魄的时刻。
特朗普宣布与委内瑞拉达成的石油协议，其合法性和透明度引发专家质疑。与此同时，委内瑞拉国内也传来批评声。
路透社独家援引美军武库知情人士报道说，美国在新近的中东伊朗冲突中，已消耗大部分高精度远程导弹库存。该消息引发了外界对美军应对未来冲突准备状态的担忧。特朗普对此类表述表达“很生气”，并威胁“严惩传播这些言论的叛徒”。

据中国人民解放军称，一架GJ-21隐形飞翼无人作战飞机（UCAV）已在076型两栖攻击舰四川舰上成功发射并回收。这一里程碑的目视确认尚未出现，但有稳定的迹象表明，配备电磁弹射器的四川号正在准备飞行试验。 GJ-21 已经被发现从陆地机场起飞。此前网上出现的一张 GJ-21 无人机的图片。中国互联网 GJ-21 及其所基于的陆基 GJ-11 神秘龙是中国在无人战斗机和其他飞翼型无人机方面进行重大投资的典型例子。这些进展与美国军方至少在公开场合回避此类设计形成鲜明对比。尽管美国过去在这一领域取得了重大成就，包括开发舰载无人战斗机，但情况仍然如此。解放军海军现在看来有望成为第一个拥有此类作战能力的国家。 076型两栖攻击舰四川舰的库存图片。解放军“中国首架舰载隐形侦察攻击无人机‘GJ-21’最近在 076 型两栖攻击舰‘四川’号（舷号 51）上首次成功起降，”解放军官方喉舌“X”上的“中国军号”账户今天发布的一篇文章称。
“这是中国两栖攻击舰发展的又一重大突破，表明中国海军现已具备在大型海上作战平台上操作固定翼隐形无人机的能力。”截至撰写本文时，解放军和中国官方媒体都没有透露这些试验发生的地点或时间，也没有提供任何其他详细信息，包括总共进行了多少次发射和回收。到目前为止，尚未发布试验的官方图片或视频。中国军号在 X 上发布的关于 GJ-21 和 076 型的帖子中附有一张图片。解放军/中国军号未经证实的说法称 GJ-21 是从四川发射的，本月早些时候已经开始在社交媒体上流传。顺便说一句，通过前起落架支柱上的弹射杆，可以很容易地将 GJ-21 与陆基 GJ-11 区分开来。两条有趣的 076 型新闻： 2. 通过 Temstar/SDF：“洋基在今晚的 Chahuahui 节目中确认 076 已经发射了 GJ-21。他也以非常直接的方式说道，基本上“你们可以停止猜测，我可以直接告诉你们：是的，他们发射了 GJ-21”。” pic.twitter.com/ODkl6Kki9A — @Rupprecht_A (@RupprechtDeino) 2026 年 10 月 15 日 对 Planet Labs 卫星图像的审查确实显示，截至 10 月 13 日，四川号仍在上海沪东中华的常规泊位，但四天后就消失了。目前尚不清楚它何时离开港口。
这艘独一无二的 076 型似乎直到 10 月 26 日才返回。TWZ 还获得了今天从 Vantor 拍摄的沪东中华号卫星图像，可以看到这艘船仍然停泊在码头上，如本文顶部和下面所示。 GJ-21 无人机，或更可能是其模型，也已经出现在码头上一段时间了。 2026 年 10 月 10 日，位于沪东中华造船厂的 076 型两栖攻击舰四川号。右图还可以看到被广泛评估为大型无人水下航行器 (UUV) 母舰的船只。卫星图像 ©2026 Vantor

【原文 English Original】
A GJ-21 stealthy flying-wing uncrewed combat air vehicle (UCAV) has successfully launched from and recovered aboard the Type 076 amphibious assault ship Sichuan , according to China’s People’s Liberation Army (PLA). Visual confirmation of this milestone has yet to emerge, but there have been steady signs of preparations for flight trials from the Sichuan , which features an electromagnetic catapult. GJ-21s have already been spotted flying from airfields on land. A picture of a GJ-21 drone that previously emerged online. Chinese internet The GJ-21 and the land-based GJ-11 Mysterious Dragon it is based on are prime examples of China’s major investments in UCAVs and other flying-wing-type drones. These developments stand in particular contrast to the U.S. military’s eschewing of such designs , at least publicly . This is despite significant past U.S. achievements in this arena, including in the development of carrier-based UCAVs. The PLA Navy (PLAN) now looks to be on track to be the first country to field an operational capability of this kind. A stock picture of the Type 076 amphibious assault ship Sichuan . PLA “China’s first ship-borne stealth reconnaissance and attack drone ‘GJ-21’ recently made its first successful take-off and landing on [the Type] 076 amphibious assault ship, the ‘Sichuan’ (Hull 51),” according to a post today from the China Military Bugle account on X, an official PLA mouthpiece. “This is another significant breakthrough in the development of China’s amphibious assault ship, indicating that the Chinese Navy now has the capability to operate fixed-wing stealth drones from large maritime combat platforms.” At the time of writing, neither the PLA nor Chinese state media have shared where or when these trials occurred or provided any other additional details, including how many total launches and recoveries were conducted. No official pictures or videos from the testing have been released so far. A graphic that accompanied the post on the China Military Bugle’s account on X regarding the GJ-21 and the Type 076. PLA/China Military Bugle Unconfirmed claims that a GJ-21 had been launched from Sichuan had already begun circulating on social media earlier this month. As an aside, the GJ-21 is readily discernible from the land-based GJ-11 by the catapult bar on its nose landing gear strut. Two interesting Type 076 News: 2. Via Temstar/SDF: "Yankee confirmed on tonight's Chahuahui that 076 has launched a GJ-21. He said it in a very straight forward way too, basically "you guys can stop guessing, I can tell you straight: yes they launched a GJ-21"." pic.twitter.com/ODkl6Kki9A — @Rupprecht_A (@RupprechtDeino) October 15, 2026 A review of satellite imagery from Planet Labs does show Sichuan was at its usual berth at Hudong-Zhonghua in Shanghai as of October 13, but absent four days later. When exactly it left port is unclear. The one-of-a-kind Type 076 does not appear to have returned until October 26. TWZ has also obtained a satellite image of Hudong-Zhonghua taken just today from Vantor, with the ship still seen sitting at the pier, as seen at the top of this story and below. GJ-21 drones, or more likely mockups thereof, have also been present on the pier for some time. The Type 076 amphibious assault ship Sichuan at the Hudong-Zhonghua shipyard on October 10, 2026. What is widely assessed to be a mothership for large uncrewed underwater vehicles (UUV) is also seen at right. Satellite image ©2026 Vantor Even while Sichuan was still under construction, there were growing signs that a navalized version of the GJ-11, as well as other uncrewed platforms, would be major components of its future air wing . With its electromagnetic catapult and notably large overall size, the Type 076 is unlike any other big-deck amphibious warship in service today globally, as TWZ has previously explored in depth . A pair of apparent GJ-11 mockups at a test and/or training site on Changxing Island in Shanghai in May 2024, near where the Type 076 was under construction at the time. Google Earth As mentioned, there have been further signs that the PLA has been preparing Sichuan for real launches and recoveries, especially of GJ-21s, since last year. Pictures emerged online in October 2025 showing a red-colored test ‘truck’ on the ship’s flight deck, indicating the start of catapult testing. Video from those tests has since been released. Weighted trucks like this have long been used to test catapults on aircraft carriers during construction  or following maintenance . The Type 076 left port for the first time in November 2025. 小紅車上線了 pic.twitter.com/zrptPDwu2X — 飞刀 (@chaoyinsukandao) October 28, 2025 Weighted carts catapult test on Type 076 LHD three lines marked directly under and outside the wheels of the Red cart to ensure it is centered the parallel alignment markings flanking the catapult slot serve as visual tips for precise positioning https://t.co/KJkC2ZrLgS pic.twitter.com/pZa0Vx56jG — David Wang (@DavidWangPLA) August 1, 2026 “Two GJ-21 aircraft were displayed at the victory parade in September 2025, reportedly having entered PLAN service in mid-2025,” according to Andreas Rupprecht , an expert on Chinese aviation and contributor to TWZ . “By late 2025, several GJ-21 aircraft were reportedly undergoing simulated EMALS launches and arrested landings at the PLAN’s land-based facility at Huangdicun .” In February of this year, GJ-21 mockups were spotted on Sichuan ’s flight deck and riding on the ship’s port-side elevator to the hangar deck as part of what appeared to be deck-handling trials. After the first Type 076 LHD/LAH "Sichuan" was seen yesterday with a GJ-21 UCAV mock-up on deck, the GJ-21 was seen for the first time with its wings folded and later lowered to the hangar deck on one of the elevators. (Images @鼎盛大彪 from Weibo) pic.twitter.com/eMyz2QLHQX — @Rupprecht_A (@RupprechtDeino) February 1, 2026 More recent satellite imagery had shown that the Type 076’s flight deck had received additional markings in line with progress toward real flight operations. Fittings for three arresting cables also became plainly visible. Those cables are also notably depicted in the graphic that the China Military Bugle shared online today. The arresting gear fittings as seen in the October 30, 2026, satellite image from Vantor, at left, as well as how they are depicted in the graphic from the China Military Bugle. Satellite image ©2026 Vantor/PLA The GJ-21 will of course not be the only aircraft in the Type 076’s future air wing. The ship is also expected to carry a variety of other uncrewed aircraft, as well as crewed helicopters. China has shown a range of other combat drone designs in recent years. Navalized versions could well be developed for deployment on Sichuan , as well as PLAN’s growing fleet of traditional carriers and other suitable configured vessels. Loading the Type 076 with operational UCAVs would only underscore the significance of this particular ship. As we have previously written : “The potential value to the PLAN of having a fleet of very large deck amphibious assault ships that are highly capable of large-scale drone operations as well as traditional amphibious assaults is clear. These ships could be used to launch and recover UCAVs like the GJ-11 and other types of drones to perform a host of missions from maritime strike to intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR). They could be used to provide additional ‘mass’ in support of the operations of larger carrier strike groups and help to free the air wings of flattops like Fujian up for tasks they might be better suited for. In addition, they could provide a lower tier of naval aviation support that could be employed independently.” … “Simply having more naval aviation capacity overall would give the PLAN added flexibility for various operations closer to the mainland, including a potential military intervention against Taiwan or defending its expansive and largely unrecognized territorial claims in places like the South China Sea . Type 076s could also help project naval and air power further from China’s shores, something that has also been a driving factor behind the country’s broader carrier ambitions .” … “The Type 076 could help provide support during humanitarian assistance and disaster relief operations. Big deck amphibious warfare ships, in general, provide their operators with immensely valuable platforms for projecting both hard and soft power .” Last year, the PLA separately confirmed that the GJ-11 had entered at least limited operational service. That followed a steady ramp-up in testing of that drone based on what could be seen in satellite imagery and video clips that had emerged online. This included evidence of near-daily flights at Malan Air Base, a  major hub for testing uncrewed platforms . GJ-11s had also been spotted at an operational air base in China’s Tibet Autonomous Region. New video out from the People's Liberation Army Air Force (PLAAF) of China shows the new GJ-11 stealth drone (UCAV), and also the J-20 stealth fighter firing a live PL-15 air-to-air missile: pic.twitter.com/wraDqyMOht — The STRATCOM Bureau (@OSPSF) November 11, 2025 As mentioned earlier, the continued development of the GJ-11 and GJ-21 are reflective of the PLA’s broader pursuit of stealthy flying-wing drones, which is not limited to UCAVs. Several larger designs that look most immediately suited to high-altitude, long-endurance ISR missions have also broken cover in the country in the past few years. There is something of a trend in this regard globally, with Russia , India , Turkey , and France also pursuing flying-wing drone designs. The U.S. military continues to be markedly absent from this space, at least that we know , despite major investments and real demonstrations of relevant capability, before various programs were abandoned for reasons that still remain largely unclear . In the late 2010s, the U.S. Navy notably looked to be right on the edge of fielding a carrier-based UCAV, before changing course entirely to an uncrewed tanker instead. There are some signs now that the service may be taking another look at the capabilities it passed over. It is still to be seen how quickly the PLA’s official statement today will be followed by real confirmation of the launching and recovery of a GJ-21 from the Sichuan . Contact the author: joe@twz.com The post Stealthy GJ-21 Drone Has Launched And Recovered From Type 076 Amphibious Assault Ship, China Claims appeared first on TWZ .

新北两名工人从吊篮坠落身亡
要激活文字转语音服务，请首先同意以下隐私政策。
中新社新北11月5日电 警方称，周四，两名工人在新北金山区省道沿线山腰进行维修工作时，从吊车吊臂上的工作篮坠落身亡。
遇难者是一名49岁的男子和他30岁的侄子。现场发现一名工人已无生命体征，另一名工人在救援人员到达时已失去知觉。警方称，两人后来在不同的医院被宣布死亡。
警方于下午 1 点 49 分接到有关这起事故的电话。初步调查确定，起重机吊臂撞击山腰，导致工人坠落。
警方称，67岁的起重机操作员和维修项目负责人被带至派出所接受讯问。
该项目由交通运输部公路局北方分局承包。
警方表示，事故原因及责任人仍在调查中。

Two workers fall to their deaths from crane basket in New Taipei

New Taipei, Nov. 5 (CNA) Two workers fell to their deaths Thursday from a work basket attached to a crane's boom while performing maintenance work on a mountainside along a provincial highway in New Taipei's Jinshan District, police said.
The victims were a 49-year-old man and his 30-year-old nephew. One worker was found with no vital signs at the scene, while the other was unconscious when rescuers arrived. Both were later pronounced dead at separate hospitals, police said.
Police received a call about the accident at 1:49 p.m. and a preliminary investigation determined that the crane's boom struck the mountainside, causing the workers to fall.
The crane operator, 67, and the person in charge of the maintenance project were taken to a police station for questioning, police said.
The project was contracted by the Highway Bureau's Northern Region Branch Office under the Ministry of Transportation and Communications.
Police said the cause of the accident and who was responsible remain under investigation.

summary: 第63屆金馬獎頒獎典禮將於11月22日於台北登場，今（5）日預告節目內容與表演卡司。圖左為部分演出嘉賓9m88，右為楊貴媚為入圍名單配音。（金馬執委會／大紀元合成） 【大紀元2026年11月05日訊】（大紀元記者馬維芬報導）第63屆金馬獎頒獎典禮將於11月22日於台北登場，5日預告節目內容與表演卡司，包含9m88、洪佩瑜和RYOTA片山凉太，及香港男團ZPOT成員Ian Hannz，都將登台獻唱入圍歌曲。此外，李佳薇將以歌聲向逝世影人致敬。金馬影后楊貴媚則獻聲錄製入圍名單。

第63屆金馬獎頒獎典禮將於11月22日於台北登場，今（5）日預告節目內容與表演卡司。圖左為部分演出嘉賓9m88，右為楊貴媚為入圍名單配音。（金馬執委會／大紀元合成）
【大紀元2026年11月05日訊】（大紀元記者馬維芬報導）第63屆金馬獎頒獎典禮將於11月22日於台北登場，5日預告節目內容與表演卡司，包含9m88、洪佩瑜和RYOTA片山凉太，及香港男團ZPOT成員Ian Hannz，都將登台獻唱入圍歌曲。此外，李佳薇將以歌聲向逝世影人致敬。金馬影后楊貴媚則獻聲錄製入圍名單。
近年影歌雙棲、表現亮眼的9m88，為參與演出並入圍九項大獎的《雙囍》譜寫演唱主題曲《輕輕放下》，以溫暖歌聲唱出主角放下糾結邁向未來人生的心情。
而洪佩瑜和RYOTA片山凉太今年以電影《黑潮》開啟合作並再度入圍，兩人將深情演唱主題曲《一去不返》；香港新銳男團成員Ian Hannz出道未滿一年，即為入圍九項大獎的《善男信女》演唱而獲得矚目，他將表演粵語主題曲《世界好壞》。
金馬63入圍歌曲表演嘉賓（左起）洪佩瑜與RYOTA片山凉太。（金馬執委會提供／大紀元合成）
金馬63入圍歌曲表演嘉賓lan Hannz。（金馬執委會提供）
除了精彩的台前演唱，曾演繹多首金曲的實力派唱將李佳薇，將以柔韌且溫暖的歌聲，向逝世影人訴說無盡的追思。
李佳薇將出席第63屆金馬獎，以柔韌而溫暖的吟唱，向逝世影人訴說無盡的追思。（金馬執委會提供）
本屆典禮幕後團隊陣容邀集多位曾獲金馬肯定的各方好手傾力貢獻所長，除了影后楊貴媚負責入圍獎項名單配音之外，曾獲金馬獎最佳美術設計得主梁碩麟再度擔任舞台美術顧問；去年獲金馬獎最佳改編劇本的潘客印，將首度操刀入圍影片集錦；知名編導徐譽庭則將特別製作短片；金馬最佳紀錄片得主楊力州亦為本屆「終身成就獎」得主虞戡平導演製作致敬影片，彰顯其卓越貢獻。

content:
台湾10月CPI上涨2.33% 连续第六个月维持在2%以上 - 焦点台湾
台湾10月CPI上涨2.33% 连续第六个月维持在2%以上
要激活文字转语音服务，请首先同意以下隐私政策。
中新社台北11月5日电 台湾主计总署周四表示，10月份台湾居民消费价格指数(CPI)同比上涨2.33%，连续第六个月保持在2%的警戒线以上。
DGBAS数据显示，不包括水果、蔬菜和能源的核心CPI同比上涨2.23%。
DGBAS官员蔡秀慧表示，CPI年率较9月份的2.74%有所放缓，主要是由于今年中秋假期在10月之后，蔬菜价格下降，电力和个人用品价格涨幅较小，以及个人护理服务费下降。
但外出就餐费用持续上涨，同比上涨3.01%，连续第五个月涨幅超过3%。
蔡表示，这一增幅比 2022 年 5.77% 的年增长率更为温和，当时俄罗斯和乌克兰战争导致价格上涨。
尽管如此，她承认外出就餐是一项常规家庭开支，这使得价格上涨对消费者来说尤其明显，并表示 DGBAS 将继续监控价格变动。
与此同时，根据DGBAS的数据，以新台币计算的台湾进口价格指数10月份同比飙升33.32%，是该指数自1977年1月推出以来的最大涨幅。
以美元计算，该指数上涨26.72%，为1980年3月以来的最大同比涨幅。
蔡将增长主要归因于矿产价格上涨58.35%，机械、电气设备及相关零件上涨31.7%，基本金属及相关产品上涨19.1%。
她表示，全球原油价格上涨推高了矿产价格，而机械和电气设备价格的上涨则反映了与人工智能相关的需求。
尽管零部件价格上涨最终可能推高包括电脑和手机在内的消费电子产品的成本，但蔡表示，大多数受影响的产品都是用于出口，限制了对国内消费者的影响。
她补充说，在全球原油价格波动的情况下，政府已采取措施稳定价格。
展望未来，蔡表示，2025年10月中秋假期期间相对较高的比较基数有助于缓和今年10月的年度CPI涨幅。
她表示，由于预计不会有长周末影响 11 月份的数据，因此 CPI 增幅可能会保持在 2% 以上，并可能超过 10 月份的 2.33%。

Taiwan's October CPI rises 2.33%, stays above 2% for sixth month - Focus Taiwan
Taiwan's October CPI rises 2.33%, stays above 2% for sixth month
To activate the text-to-speech service, please first agree to the privacy policy below.
Taipei, Nov. 5 (CNA) Taiwan's consumer price index (CPI) rose 2.33 percent year-on-year in October, remaining above the 2 percent alert threshold for the sixth consecutive month, the Directorate General of Budget, Accounting and Statistics (DGBAS) said Thursday.
Core CPI, which excludes fruit, vegetables and energy, increased 2.23 percent from a year earlier, according to DGBAS data.
DGBAS official Tsai Hsiu-hui (蔡秀慧) said the annual CPI growth rate eased from 2.74 percent in September, mainly due to lower vegetable prices, smaller increases in electricity and personal goods prices, and a decline in personal care service fees, as the Mid-Autumn Festival holiday fell outside October this year.
However, dining-out costs continued to rise, increasing 3.01 percent year-on-year and marking the fifth consecutive month of growth above 3 percent.
Tsai said the increase was more moderate than the 5.77 percent annual growth recorded in 2022, when prices were driven higher by the Russia-Ukraine war.
Nevertheless, she acknowledged that dining out is a regular household expense, making price increases particularly noticeable to consumers, and said the DGBAS would continue to monitor price movements.
Meanwhile, Taiwan's import price index, measured in New Taiwan dollar terms, surged 33.32 percent year-on-year in October, its largest increase since the index was introduced in January 1977, according to the DGBAS.
In U.S. dollar terms, the index rose 26.72 percent, its steepest year-on-year increase since March 1980.
Tsai attributed the increase mainly to higher prices for minerals, which rose 58.35 percent, machinery, electrical equipment and related parts, up 31.7 percent, and basic metals and related products, up 19.1 percent.
She said mineral prices were pushed higher by rising global crude oil prices, while increases in machinery and electrical equipment prices reflected demand related to artificial intelligence.
Although higher component prices could eventually push up the cost of consumer electronics, including computers and mobile phones, Tsai said most of the affected products were intended for export, limiting the impact on domestic consumers.
She added that the government had taken measures to stabilize prices amid fluctuations in global crude oil prices.
Looking ahead, Tsai said the relatively high comparison base in October 2025, when the Mid-Autumn Festival holiday took place, had helped moderate this October's annual CPI increase.
With no long weekends expected to affect November's figures, she said CPI growth was likely to remain above 2 percent and could exceed October's 2.33 percent.

zh_title: 中期选举后可能面临更大的加速对台军售的压力
summary: 中期选举后加速对台军售可能面临更大压力海峡时报 中期选举后，加速对台军售的压力可能更大席卷美国中期选举的浪潮可能会给白宫带来更大压力，要求其批准价值 140 亿美元（178.6 亿新元）的军备
content:
中期选举后加速对台军售可能面临更大压力海峡时报
中期选举后可能面临更大的加速对台军售的压力
立即注册：深入了解亚洲的快速发展
11 月 3 日，支持者庆祝民主党州长候选人吉娜·伊诺霍萨在德克萨斯州获胜。
发表于 2026 年 11 月 5 日，下午 06:30
更新于 2026 年 11 月 5 日，晚上 8:17
台北 — — 席卷美国中期选举的民主党蓝潮可能会给白宫带来更大压力，迫使其批准价值 140 亿美元（178.6 亿新元）的对台军售计划，这对台湾来说是一个可喜的结果。
唐纳德·特朗普总统的共和党政府已放慢了对自治台湾的军售，将其视为与中国打交道的“谈判”筹码，而中国则反对此类军售，因为它认为台湾是其领土，可以在必要时通过武力与大陆统一。
与此同时，台湾坚称该岛处理与美国关系的态度是无党派的。
台湾外交部11月5日对《海峡时报》表示，台湾与美国的关系基于“无党派接触、广泛善意和积极沟通的原则，长期以来得到美国国会和行政部门两党议员的一贯支持”。
在此基础上，外交部将继续深化同美方在安全、贸易、科技、教育等各领域的全面合作。
国防部长顾维灵顿在立法机关出席会议时对记者表示：“美国国会在两党的基础上一贯支持台湾加强防御能力的努力。”
他补充道：“我们还将继续与国会议员沟通，当然我们也会与美国陆军部保持密切联系，以确保这些相关军售如期进行。”
事实上，专家预计中期选举后特朗普将面临更大的军售计划压力。
美国外交关系委员会亚洲研究高级研究员戴维·萨克斯表示：“我确实认为，中期选举的一个结果可能是共和党人开始在这个问题上与特朗普总统决裂，并在这个问题上采取更加独立的立场，并开始向政府施加压力，要求其批准这些军售。”
他在新闻流媒体平台“台湾+”上表示，国会可以尝试将六项保证写入立法。 1982年7月，罗纳德·里根总统的政府将“六项保证”秘密转交台北，随后解密。
其中包括一项不设定终止对台军售日期的条款，旨在在1982年美中谈判达成军售联合公报后安抚台湾，该公报表示美国不会寻求长期军售政策，并将逐步减少对台军售。
萨克斯表示，国会将传递这样一个信息：“我们无法控制特朗普总统的言论，但至少台湾和世界各国应该明白，他不一定反映美国对此的主流想法”。
尽管美国数十个城市的选民在中期选举期间批准了对数据中心的限制或彻底禁令，但分析人士认为，台湾向美国出口数据中心相关硬件的影响不大。
Roy Lee，高级部门

Greater pressure to speed up arms sales to Taiwan possible after midterms | The Straits Times
Greater pressure to speed up arms sales to Taiwan possible after midterms
Sign up now: Get insights on Asia's fast-moving developments
Supporters celebrate Democratic gubernatorial candidate Gina Hinojosa's win in Texas on Nov 3.
Published Nov 05, 2026, 06:30 PM
Updated Nov 05, 2026, 08:17 PM
TAIPEI – In what would be a welcome outcome for Taiwan, the Democratic blue wave that swept the US midterm elections could see greater pressure on the White House to approve a US$14 billion (S$17.86 billion) arms sales package to the island.
President Donald Trump’s Republican administration has slowed down arms sales to self-ruled Taiwan, seeing these as a “negotiating” chip in its dealings with China, which opposes such sales as it sees Taiwan as its territory to be reunified with the mainland, by force if necessary.
Taiwan, meanwhile, has maintained that the island’s approach to relations with the United States is non-partisan.
Taiwan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) told The Straits Times on Nov 5 that the island’s relations with the US are based on “a principle of non-partisan engagement, fostering broad goodwill, and active communication, which has long enjoyed consistent support from bipartisan members of the US Congress and the executive branch”.
Building on this foundation, MOFA will continue to deepen comprehensive cooperation with the US in various fields, including security, trade, science and technology, and education, it added.
Speaking to reporters at the legislature where he was attending a session, Defence Minister Wellington Koo said: “The US Congress has consistently supported – on a bipartisan basis – Taiwan’s efforts to beef up its defence capabilities.”
He added: “We will also continue to communicate with members of Congress, and of course we will maintain close contact with the US Department of War to ensure that these related arms sales proceed on schedule.”
Indeed, experts expected pressure on Trump to rise over the arms sales package post midterms.
“I do think that one outcome to the midterm elections could be that Republicans start to break with President Trump on this question, and have... a more independent position on this and do start to raise pressure on the administration to approve those arms sales,” said David Sacks, senior fellow for Asia studies at the Council on Foreign Relations.
Speaking to the news streaming platform Taiwan Plus, he noted that Congress could try to codify the Six Assurances into legislation. The Six Assurances were conveyed to Taipei privately in July 1982 by the administration of President Ronald Reagan, and later declassified.
They include a clause to not set a date for ending arms sales to Taiwan, and were meant to reassure Taiwan after the 1982 Joint Communique on Arms Sales was negotiated between the US and China that said the US would not seek a long-term arms sales policy and would gradually reduce its arms sales to Taiwan.
Sacks said Congress would be sending a message that “we can’t control what President Trump says, but at least Taiwan and countries around the world should understand that he doesn’t necessarily reflect mainstream US thinking on this”.
While voters in dozens of American cities approved restrictions or outright bans on data centres during the midterm elections, analysts saw little impact on Taiwan’s exports of data centre-related hardware to the US.
Roy Lee, a senior deputy executive director and associate research fellow at the Chung-Hua Institution for Economic Research’s Center for International Trade Policy, told Focus Taiwan that there will be continued growth in demand in artificial intelligence.
Therefore, a slowdown in the data centre build-out in the US is not likely to have significant impact on Taiwanese hardware suppliers.
“There may be a slight slowdown in expansion in the short term, but the overall direction has not changed,” Focus Taiwan reported Lee as saying.

content:
Somalia Condemns Israel's Appointment of Ambassador to Hargeisa, Embassy Construction Move - allAfrica.com
Somalia Condemns Israel's Appointment of Ambassador to Hargeisa, Embassy Construction Move
Somaliland President Abdirahman Mohamed Abdullahi Irro plants a symbolic tree at the Groves of Nations in Jerusalem on June 15, 2026. The tree represents friendship, cooperation and the growing relationship between Somaliland and Israel.
Mogadishu — Somalia's Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation has strongly condemned Israel's reported appointment of an ambassador to Hargeisa and the laying of a foundation stone for a building it described as an embassy in the Somali territory.
In a statement, the ministry said the moves, taken without the consent of the Federal Government of Somalia, constituted a violation of the country's sovereignty, unity and territorial integrity.
The ministry described the actions as null and void, saying they carried no legal effect. It reaffirmed that Hargeisa and the northwestern regions remain an integral part of the Federal Republic of Somalia.
Somalia's Foreign Ministry said the establishment of diplomatic relations and the opening of permanent diplomatic missions require the consent of the sovereign state concerned, in accordance with the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations.
Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn
It added that no unilateral action could override these requirements or alter the status of Somali territory.
The ministry said the latest developments followed Israel's recognition of Somaliland, announced in December 2025, which it said had been rejected by the African Union, the Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD), the Arab League and the Organization of Islamic Cooperation.
It warned that actions encouraging fragmentation and disregarding internationally recognized borders could further heighten security tensions in the region, particularly around the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden.
Somalia called on Israel to immediately reverse the measures and urged governments and international organizations to reject them and avoid any action that could lend them legitimacy.
The government also said it reserved the right to take appropriate diplomatic, political and legal measures, in accordance with international law, to defend the country's sovereignty, unity and territorial integrity.
The ministry concluded by stressing that Somalia's sovereignty and territorial integrity must be respected, adding that the unity of the Somali people was not open to negotiation.

content:
第二十一篇：顺服生命的感觉——随从灵而行，经历生命与平安 – 罗兰岗召会 Church In Rowland Heights
親愛的弟兄姊妹：初信的弟兄姊妹常问：我怎样知道主的引导？我怎样知道这件事合不合主的心意？答案不全在外面，乃在里面：神重生我们的时候，在我们里面放了一个新的感觉，就是生命的感觉。我们学习顺服这个感觉，就是学习随从灵而行。
罗马书八章六节，把两个心思、两个结果说得清清楚楚：“因为心思置于肉体，就是死；心思置于灵，乃是生命，又是平安。”心思放在哪里，感觉就在哪里：放在灵里，是生命，又是平安；放在肉体里，是死亡的感觉。初信生活最要紧的功课，就是学习把心思置于灵，顺服灵里生命的感觉。
我们里面为什么有感觉？因为神的生命进来了，生命有它的律。罗马书八章二节说：“因为生命之灵的律，在基督耶稣里已经释放了我，使我脱离了罪与死的律。”生命之灵的律，是自发自动的，如同心脏的跳动、种子的生长，不需要我们指挥，它自己会运行：合乎生命的，它给我们平安通畅的感觉；违背生命的，它给我们受阻不安的感觉。
约翰一书二章二十七节，又说到膏油的涂抹：“你们从他所受的膏油涂抹，住在你们里面，并不需要人教导你们，乃有他的膏油涂抹，在凡事上教导你们；这膏油涂抹是真实的，不是虚谎的，你们要按这膏油涂抹所教导你们的，住在他里面。”
膏油涂抹在凡事上教导我们——不是教道理，乃是借着里面的运行给我们感觉：涂抹得通畅，我们就平安；涂抹受阻挡，我们就不安。这是初信者最实际的引导：主不需要天天从天上说话，祂已经住在我们里面，用生命的感觉和膏油的运行，作我们随时的引导。
生命的感觉有两面。消极的一面是死亡的感觉：一件事还没有作，里面先不平安；一句话刚出口，里面就沉重、干枯、黑暗、懊悔；一个地方还没去，里面就受搅扰、没有安息。这些感觉不是心情不好，这是里面生命在抗议：这件事不合生命，这条路不通。积极的一面是生命平安的感觉：顺从里面引导的时候，里面清明、舒畅、刚强、满足，越走越有供应，越行越有平安。
罗马书八章十四节说：“因为凡被神的灵引导的，都是神的儿子。”被灵引导的人，是神的儿子：儿子的记号不是知道多少道理，乃是能被灵引导。约翰福音十章二十七节，主说：“我的羊听我的声音，我也认识他们，他们也跟着我来。”羊认得牧人的声音，不是因为懂得多，乃是因为有生命的本能。初信者不要轻看里面微小的感觉：那正是牧人的声音，是生命的本能在你里面运行。
顺服生命的感觉，有一个要紧的原则：不要用头脑去推翻它。里面的感觉常常没有理由，说不出道理，却准确无比：你讲得出十个理由去作一件事，只要里面不平安，就不要作；等到平安回来，再作不迟。
歌罗西书三章十五节，给我们一位里面的仲裁者：“又要让基督的平安在你们心里作仲裁，你们在一个身体里蒙召，也是为了这平安；且要成为感谢的人。”基督的平安在心里作仲裁——像裁判一样：平安在，这件事过关；平安不在，这件事出局。决定大小事，都让平安作最后的裁判：在平安里作的决定，事后多有印证；在不安里硬作的决定，事后多要收拾。
腓立比书四章七节说，这平安还要保守我们：“神那超越人所能理解的平安，必在基督耶稣里，保卫你们的心怀意念。”我们也要留心：生命的感觉越顺服就越敏锐，越抗拒就越迟钝。今天在一件小事上顶撞它，明天它就不那么清楚了；今天在小感觉上顺服它，明天它在大事上就更明亮。
希伯来书五章十四节说到成熟的分辨力：“惟独长大成人的，才能吃干粮，他们的官能因习用而练达，就能分辨好坏了。”官能因习用而练达——生命的感觉是操练出来的：天天习用，天天顺服，官能就练达，分辨就准确。
加拉太书五章十六节和二十五节，给我们随从灵而行的实行：“我说，你们当凭着灵而行，就绝不会满足肉体的情欲了。”“我们若凭着灵活着，也就当凭着灵而行。”凭着灵活着是地位，凭着灵而行是生活。怎样随从灵而行？第一，把心思置于灵：借着祷读主话、呼求主名，让心思从外面的人事物转回到灵里（罗八6）。第二，在小事上跟随感觉：一句话要说，先问里面平安不平安；一个地方要去、一件东西要买、一个约要赴，都让里面的感觉过目。第三，即时顺服：感觉一来就停、就来祷告，不要拖延，不要讨价还价。初信者最美的见证就在这里：不凭自己的聪明，不随自己的喜好，只凭里面生命的感觉而行——行在生命里，就经历生命；行在平安里，就得享平安。
弟兄姊妹，我们要一同开口、一同宣告：我们要顺服生命的感觉！我们要把心思置于灵，不置于肉体；我们要让基督的平安在心里作仲裁，凭着灵而行，不凭自己而行。我们要经历生命，又经历平安，从初信的日子起，就走在随从灵的路上！
禱告：哦主耶稣，我们为你住在我们里面感谢你！你用生命之灵的律运行我们，用膏油涂抹教导我们，用平安在我们心里作仲裁。求你使我们敏锐于生命的感觉：在死亡的感觉里立刻停下，在生命平安的感觉里勇敢跟随；使我们天天凭着灵而行，经历生命与平安，作一群被你的灵引导的神的儿女。阿们，哈利路亚！
我虽然行过死荫的幽谷，也不怕遭害，因为你与我同在；你的杖，你的竿，都安慰我。
在我敌人面前，你为我摆设筵席；你用油膏了我的头，使我的福杯满溢。
我一生一世必有恩惠慈爱随着我，我且要住在耶和华的殿中，直到永远。

summary: 尽管工资委员会有所变动，孟加拉国服装抗议仍在继续尽管工资委员会发生了变化，但孟加拉国的服装抗议活动仍在继续。立即注册：了解亚洲快速发展的发展。在工人们堵塞高速公路并投掷砖块后，警方在阿苏利亚使用了催泪瓦斯和声波手榴弹。发布于 2026 年 11 月 5 日，晚上 10:03 更新于 2026 年 11 月 5 日，晚上 10:59 尽管工资委员会采取行动，从 12 月开始修改工资结构，但孟加拉国的服装工人在 11 月 5 日继续抗议。工人们封锁高速公路并投掷炸弹后，警方在阿苏利亚使用了催泪瓦斯和声波手榴弹。
content:
尽管工资委员会有所变动，孟加拉国服装抗议仍在继续海峡时报
尽管工资委员会有所变动，孟加拉国服装抗议仍在继续
立即注册：深入了解亚洲的快速发展

发布于 2026 年 11 月 5 日，晚上 10:03
更新于 2026 年 11 月 5 日，晚上 10:59
尽管工资委员会从 12 月起调整工资结构，但孟加拉国的制衣工人在 11 月 5 日仍继续抗议。
在阿苏利亚，工人们封锁高速公路并投掷砖块后，警方使用了催泪瓦斯和声波手榴弹； 100多家工厂关闭，引发了出口延迟的担忧。
工人们希望将最低月工资从 12,500 塔卡提高到 30,000 塔卡，因为生活成本上涨影响了工资，而且动乱威胁到了该行业的低成本出口优势。
达卡—11 月 5 日，孟加拉国服装工人发起新的抗议活动，迫使工厂暂停运营，尽管工资委员会已采取行动，从 12 月起引入修订后的工资结构。
10 月 31 日开始的抗议活动已迫使数百家工厂关闭，生产中断，并引发了人们对孟加拉国这个仅次于中国的全球第二大服装出口国的出口运输延误的担忧。
工人们最初于 11 月 5 日早些时候在首都达卡郊区的主要服装制造中心阿苏利亚报到上班。但他们后来走出去并封锁了一条主要高速公路，要求明确宣布拟议的加薪。
阿舒利亚工业警察总监穆罕默德·莫米努·伊斯兰·布伊扬 (Mohammad Mominul Islam Bhuiyan) 表示：“抗议者向警察投掷砖块并破坏警车后，我们不得不使用催泪瓦斯和声波手榴弹。”
他说，11 月 5 日该地区有 100 多家工厂暂停运营，并补充说，已在工业区部署了更多警察和孟加拉国边境警卫队人员，以防止进一步的骚乱。
与此同时，其他工业中心的情况相对平静，包括萨瓦尔和加济布尔，尽管一些工厂仍暂时关闭，但许多工人重返工作岗位。
由于安全部队在主要工业区保持高度戒备，当局已敦促工厂员工重返工作岗位。
工资委员会于 11 月 4 日同意从 12 月起实施修订后的工资结构，工人将于 1 月收到新工资标准下的第一笔工资。但尚未确定增加的规模。
工人们要求将最低月工资从目前的 12,500 塔卡增加一倍多至 30,000 塔卡（308 新元），称食品、住房和交通成本上涨削弱了他们的购买力。
“所有东西的价格都上涨了，但工资却没有。维持收支平衡变得越来越困难，”没有参加 11 月 5 日抗议活动的服装工人 Shilpi Khatun 说。
低工资和进入主要西方市场的免税准入有助于推动孟加拉国服装业的增长，该行业占这个南亚国家80%以上的出口收入，但骚乱正在考验其低成本优势。
该行业雇佣了约 400 万名工人，并为 H&M、Zara 所有者 Inditex 和沃尔玛等全球主要品牌供货。制造商警告称，骚乱可能会扰乱出口订单旺季的生产计划。路透社

Bangladesh garment protests continue despite wage board move
Sign up now: Get insights on Asia's fast-moving developments
The police used tear gas and sound grenades in Ashulia after workers blocked a highway and threw bricks.
Published Nov 05, 2026, 10:03 PM
Updated Nov 05, 2026, 10:59 PM
Garment workers in Bangladesh kept protesting on Nov 5, despite a wage board move to bring in a revised pay structure from December.
Police used tear gas and sound grenades in Ashulia after workers blocked a highway and threw bricks; more than 100 factories shut, raising export delay fears.
Workers want the minimum monthly wage raised to 30,000 taka from 12,500, as rising living costs hit pay, and unrest threatens the sector’s low-cost export edge.
DHAKA – Garment workers staged fresh protests in Bangladesh on Nov 5, forcing factories to suspend operations despite a wage board move to introduce a revised pay structure from December.
The protests, which began on Oct 31, have forced the closure of hundreds of factories, disrupting production and raising concerns about export shipment delays in Bangladesh, the world’s second-largest garment exporter after China.
Workers initially reported to work early on Nov 5 in Ashulia, a major garment manufacturing hub on the outskirts of the capital Dhaka. But they later walked out and blocked a major highway, demanding a clear announcement on the proposed wage increase.
“We had to use tear gas and sound grenades after protesters threw bricks at police and vandalised police vehicles,” Ashulia Industrial Police Superintendent Mohammad Mominul Islam Bhuiyan said.
More than 100 factories suspended operations in the area on Nov 5, he said, adding that additional police and Border Guard Bangladesh personnel had been deployed across the industrial zone to prevent further unrest.
The situation was, meanwhile, relatively calm in other industrial hubs, including Savar and Gazipur where many workers returned to their jobs, though some factories remained temporarily closed.
The authorities have urged factory employees to come back to work as security forces remain on high alert across major industrial zones.
The wage board agreed on Nov 4 to implement a revised wage structure from December, with workers set to receive their first pay under the new scale in January. But it has yet to determine the size of the increase.
Workers are demanding that the minimum monthly wage be more than doubled to 30,000 taka (S$308) from 12,500 taka currently, saying rising food, housing and transport costs have eroded their purchasing power.
“The prices of everything have gone up, but wages have not. It is becoming harder and harder to make ends meet,” said Shilpi Khatun, a garment worker who did not join the Nov 5 protest.
Low wages and duty-free access to key Western markets helped fuel the growth of Bangladesh’s garment industry, which generates more than 80% of the South Asian nation’s export earnings, but the unrest is testing its low-cost advantage.
The sector employs about 4 million workers and supplies major global brands including H&M, Zara owner Inditex and Walmart. Manufacturers warn the unrest could disrupt production schedules during the peak season for export orders. REUTERS

Completing a Master of Science in Nutrition as a Registered Dietitian Nutritionist prepared Lisa for working in the medical sector assisting patients with a variety of illnesses, disease states, and conditions. During this time to the present, Lisa pursued further studies in alternative and integrative health practices attaining multiple credentials. While working in these areas, Lisa continued serving in her roles as a mother, daughter, sister, and friend.
Sounds Productive Right? Does Being More Productive Support Health and Well-Being?
“Getting busier does not necessarily make you better…affectively managing your stress does!”
You really didn’t think all of that activity was done perfectly with complete ease and grace, did you? Of course not. As Lisa was stressed out creating elevated levels of cortisol and adrenaline, this lack of balance was in opposition to a positive state of health and well-being. How ironic is that behavior? Lisa more fully understands how stress and being out of balance can have a negative impact on the mind and body. Sometimes the vehicle that drives a person to do, may eventually run them over. Hypothetically speaking, imagine being in a hit and run accident driven by yourself in your very own car. Can you relate now? The coping mechanism of burning the candle at both ends is comfortable because it is familiar. However, the candle may eventually burn out.
If there is one commonality that we all have in this human experience, it’s managing our own life stressors. Add a dose or two of trauma along the way and what do you get…Amplified Stress with Triggers. The well-being sessions are offered here for interested participants to explore complementary and integrative approaches on processing and managing stress to ultimately feel and function better. You are invited to take this peaceful exploration on optimizing your own health and happiness.
